page.title: Marbella Boat Rental vs Estepona Charter 2028: Marina Comparison

data.meta_description: Marbella boat rental vs Estepona charter 2028: compare marinas, distances, nightlife & prices. Find which base suits your day on the Costa del Sol.
data.summary: Compare Marbella boat rental vs Estepona charter in 2028: Puerto Banús offers luxury, nightlife, and shorter runs to Cala del Faro, while Estepona gives quieter waters and quicker access to Sotogrande. Choose based on your group’s vibe and budget.

faq.q: Which is cheaper: Marbella boat rental or Estepona charter?
faq.a: Our fleet operates exclusively from Puerto Banús, Marbella, so we only quote Marbella prices. Rates start at €749/2h for an Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (skipper, drinks, VAT included). Estepona charter prices are typically similar for comparable boats, but you’ll pay more in fuel if you want to reach the same anchorages as from Banús.

faq.q: How far is Estepona from Puerto Banús by boat?
faq.a: It’s about 12 nautical miles west along the coast. At cruising speed (20–25 knots), that’s roughly 30–35 minutes. Most day charters from Puerto Banús head east to Cala del Faro or Cabopino, so Estepona is only a short detour if you want to explore both.

faq.q: Which marina has better nightlife after a boat trip?
faq.a: Puerto Banús is the nightlife capital of the Costa del Sol, with dozens of clubs, bars, and restaurants right on the waterfront. Estepona marina is quieter, with a few decent terraces but no clubbing scene. If your group wants to party after the charter, Marbella boat rental is the clear choice.

faq.q: Can I anchor near Estepona on a Marbella boat rental?
faq.a: Yes. The coastline between Marbella and Estepona has several sandy coves, including Playa del Saladillo and Playa de la Salida. Estepona’s own beaches are wide and less crowded than Marbella’s. Your skipper will know the best spots based on wind and swell.

faq.q: Is the Mangusta 80 available for Estepona departures?
faq.a: No. The Mangusta 80 (both white and grey variants) departs exclusively from Puerto Banús. At 24m and 12 pax, it’s ideal for groups who want a free jet ski included. The minimum charter is 4 hours at €4,719. You can still cruise west to Estepona during your trip.

faq.q: Which has better weather: Marbella or Estepona?
faq.a: Both enjoy the same microclimate: 320+ sunny days a year, average 22°C in summer. Estepona can be slightly breezier in the afternoon due to the Poniente wind funneling through the Strait. Marbella’s bay is more sheltered, so sea conditions are often calmer.

faq.q: How do I book a boat from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Contact us via WhatsApp for any boat not listed with fixed prices. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), you can book directly online. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and Spanish VAT. No hidden fees.

faq.q: What’s the difference in cruising range between the two marinas?
faq.a: From Puerto Banús, you can reach Cala del Faro (15 min), Cabopino (20 min), Marbella Marina (10 min), and Estepona (35 min). From Estepona, you’re closer to Sotogrande (20 min) and Gibraltar (45 min). For most day trips, Marbella boat rental gives you more variety in less time.

data.body_html:
Planning a day on the water along the Costa del Sol often comes down to one choice: Marbella boat rental vs Estepona charter. Both marinas offer access to the same Mediterranean coastline, but the vibe, logistics, and cruising options differ. This 2028 comparison breaks down the key factors so you can pick the right base for your group — whether you want a party on the water or a peaceful anchorage near Sotogrande.

Puerto Banús vs Estepona Marina: Location & Access

Puerto Banús sits at the heart of Marbella’s Golden Mile, 5 minutes from the city centre and surrounded by luxury boutiques and nightlife. Estepona Marina (Puerto Deportivo de Estepona) is about 12 nautical miles west, closer to Sotogrande and Gibraltar. Both have fuel docks, chandlers, and restaurants, but Puerto Banús is larger and busier. If you want to step off the boat straight into a club, choose Marbella. If you prefer a quieter start to your day, Estepona works well.

Cruising Distances & Anchorages

From Puerto Banús, you can reach Cala del Faro in 15 minutes, Cabopino in 20, and Marbella’s town beach in 10. Heading west, Estepona is 30–35 minutes. From Estepona, Sotogrande is 20 minutes, and Gibraltar is 45. For a half-day charter, Marbella gives you more anchorages in less time. Our boat rental Marbella fleet departs exclusively from Puerto Banús, so you get the widest choice of coves without long transfers.

Fleet Options & Pricing

Our fleet from Puerto Banús includes 16 boats from 6.4m to 29m. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749/2h or €2,299/8h — all inclusive. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is €4,719 for 4 hours with a free jet ski. Other boats like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86 are priced on request via WhatsApp. Estepona charter operators have similar boats but often charge extra for fuel or skipper. Our prices include everything: skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT.

Nightlife & Onshore Amenities

Puerto Banús is famous for its after-dark scene: Ocean Club, Pangea, and dozens of beach bars are within walking distance of the marina. Estepona’s old town has charming tapas bars but no clubbing. If your charter ends at sunset and you want to keep the party going, Marbella boat rental is the obvious pick. For a relaxed dinner by the water, Estepona is fine.

Sea Conditions & Weather

Both areas enjoy 320+ sunny days per year. Sea temperature averages 22°C from July to September, dropping to 16°C in April. Marbella’s bay is more sheltered from the Poniente wind, so the water is often calmer. Estepona can get a light chop in the afternoon. For families or those prone to seasickness, Marbella is the safer bet.

Which Base Suits Your Group?

Choose Marbella boat rental if: you want a party, you’re staying on the Golden Mile, or you want quick access to Cala del Faro and Cabopino. Choose Estepona charter if: you’re staying in Sotogrande or Gibraltar, you prefer quiet beaches, or you’re on a tighter budget for marina fees (though our prices are the same regardless). Both give you a fantastic day on the water — the difference is in the details.
